source.anchor_kjv: My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me?
source.thread: Jesus' cry from the cross (Matthew 27:46) is verbatim Psalm 22:1 — the opening line David wrote ~1000 years early. The strongest link in the series: Jesus did not merely match the psalm, He deliberately QUOTED its first sentence. The cry of dereliction is the sinless Son taking our place and bearing the forsaking our sin deserved — so that you never will be forsaken.
source.thread_lever: NT-confirmed OT echo (Jesus quotes the verse Himself; no textual variant)
source.hook_line: The loneliest sentence Jesus ever spoke wasn't his own line.
source.spoken_script: The loneliest sentence Jesus ever spoke wasn't his own line. He was quoting, Psalm 22 opens in the voice of a forsaken man. David wrote it, Jesus made it his own. David's very first line, my God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me? A thousand years later, at the ninth hour, Jesus cried it from the cross. My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me? The very same words. This was no cry of lost faith. Even forsaken, he still calls God, my God. It was the sinless Son taking our place and bearing the forsaking that our sin deserved. He was forsaken so that you never will be. However far you've run, the way home is open, and he opened it from the dark.

platforms.title: The Loneliest Sentence He Ever Spoke Was Not His Own Line
platforms.description:
The loneliest sentence Jesus ever spoke wasn't his own line. He was quoting.

Psalm 22:1 (KJV): "My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me?"

David wrote it a thousand years before. At the ninth hour, Jesus cried those exact words from the cross. Not a coincidence - a deliberate quotation. He opened the psalm on purpose.

Even in that moment, he still called God his God. This was not a cry of lost faith. It was the sinless Son taking our place, bearing the forsaking our sin deserved.

He was forsaken so that you never will be. The way home is open. He opened it from the dark.

platforms.label: YouTube (Long-form 16:9)
platforms.title: Psalm 22:1 - Why Jesus Cried 'My God, My God' from the Cross
platforms.description:
At the ninth hour, Jesus cried the loneliest sentence in human history. But it wasn't his own line.

Psalm 22:1 (KJV): "My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me?"

David wrote those words a thousand years before. Jesus quoted them verbatim from the cross (Matthew 27:46). He didn't just match the psalm - he opened it. He was quoting it on purpose, pointing everyone who knew the text to what was happening.

Notice: even forsaken, he still said my God. This was not a cry of lost faith or abandoned theology. It was the sinless Son taking our place, bearing the forsaking that our sin deserved. The wrath that should have been ours.

He was forsaken so that you never will be. However far you have run, the way home is open. He opened it from the dark.

Psalm 22 | Matthew 27 | KJV
